correctness.rationale: Odd order makes inversion free on every nonprincipal dual character, so nonlinear irreducibles are exactly the induced inversion pairs. For such a pair, the induced character has degree two, vanishes outside the kernel subgroup, and has kernel equal to the inducing character's kernel; hence its codegree is the inducing character's exact order. The dual group is isomorphic to the abelian kernel, giving multiplicity N_A(d)/2. Finally, the counts of elements of order dividing p^k recover the partition of every abelian p-primary component. The packaged checker independently verifies both the pseudo-algebra formula and the reconstruction algorithm.

Lewis--Yan's 2024 follow-up gives global p-group counterexamples and p-group rigidity conditions; its indexed searchable text likewise contains no generalized-dihedral or Frobenius theorem. value.rationale: Group pseudo-algebras are known not to determine even group order in general, so a complete rigidity theorem for a broad nonabelian family is structurally meaningful. The result gives more than an isomorphism criterion: it identifies the exact information encoded by every multiplicity and provides an explicit Sylow-by-Sylow reconstruction algorithm. Generalized dihedral groups are a canonical nonabelian extension of abelian groups, making this a natural test family for the pseudo-algebra program.
